meta.title: Ch 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 3 (Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements).

questions.q: Ind AS 1 requires an entity to present a third balance sheet when:
o: Retrospective application of an accounting policy occurs
The entity reports a loss in either comparative year
Segmental information is disclosed for two segments
questions.why: The third statement of financial position (as at the beginning of the earliest comparative period) is required only on retrospective application/restatement/reclassification affecting the balance sheet — not merely because comparatives exist.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — trigger-condition questions on Ind AS 1 recur every attempt Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: 3rd balance sheet = only for retro policy change, restatement or reclass. Think: does the OPENING figure itself move?

questions.q: An entity has a loan due 31 March 20X7. By 25 February 20X7 the lender agrees not to demand repayment despite a covenant breach, without any condition. How is the loan classified in Ind AS financial statements for the year ended 31 March 20X7?
o: Current — the breach makes it callable
Non-current — no right to demand payment existed at the reporting date, and the agreement removed the breach effect before the reporting date
Current, because the concession came after the reporting date
Non-current only if the loan is restructured with a rate cut
questions.why: Where the lender agrees BEFORE the reporting date not to demand payment as a consequence of a covenant breach, the classification is non-current (the loan is not then payable at the reporting date's demand). Concessions occurring after the reporting date are non-adjusting events (Ind AS 10).
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — covenants + classification timing is exactly the Ind AS 1 trap ICAI likes AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Date discipline: agreement before reporting date = non-current; after = still current (non-adjusting). The reporting date is the full stop.

questions.q: The tax base of an expense that will be deductible for tax purposes only when it is PAID in a future period, recognised as an accrued liability, is:
o: Nil for both book and tax
questions.why: Where an expense will be deductible only when paid, the liability's tax base equals its carrying amount LESS the amount deductible in future periods — i.e. future deductible amount (often resulting in a tax base of carrying amount minus deduction). The framework defines tax base as the amount attributed to the liability for tax purposes: carrying amount less future tax deductions.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — deferred-tax mechanics of accrued expenses are recurring Section B candidates Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Tax base of a liability = amount deductible later. Accrued expense deductible on payment ⇒ tax base = CA − future deduction ⇒ DTA. Trace the money to the tax return, not to the book.

questions.q: Goodwill arising on a business combination under Ind AS 103 has a carrying amount of Rs 80 crore and a tax base of Rs 50 crore (amortisation allowed for tax). The initial-recognition exemption in Ind AS 12 for the resulting Rs 30 crore taxable temporary difference:
o: Applies — no deferred tax liability is recognised on goodwill's initial recognition
Does not apply to goodwill; a DTL of Rs 7.5 crore (at 25%) must be recognised
Applies because goodwill is not amortised for accounting
Only applies in separate financial statements
questions.why: Ind AS 12 explicitly EXCLUDES goodwill from the initial-recognition exemption; a DTL on the taxable temporary difference arising on initial recognition of goodwill is recognised (with the consequential increase to goodwill), here 25% × 30 = 7.5 crore.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the goodwill carve-out is the classic ICAI 'exemption does NOT apply' question AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Initial-recognition exemption: exists for most assets/liabilities, but NEVER for goodwill. DTL on goodwill adds to goodwill — a small circle, allow it.

questions.q: Assets and liabilities may be offset in the balance sheet when:
o: The entity intends to settle on a gross basis
There is a legally enforceable right to offset AND intention for net settlement or simultaneous realisation
questions.why: Ind AS 1/32 offsetting needs BOTH a legally enforceable right and net-simultaneous intent — not merely net exposure or practice.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — conjunctive-condition MCQ — quick and deadly Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Offsetting needs two keys: legal right + intent to net/simultaneous settlement. One key doesn't open it.

questions.q: A prior-period depreciation was calculated using the wrong asset life due to a mathematical mistake. This is:
o: Prior period error — retrospective restatement of comparatives
questions.why: Mathematical mistakes/misapplication of policies = errors ⇒ retrospective restatement; changes in estimate are prospective.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the error-vs-estimate boundary is tested to death AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Error = rewind and restate; estimate = drift forward. Math mistake is an error, never an estimate.

questions.q: Current/non-current classification of an asset generally requires it to be realised within:
o: 12 months after the reporting period, or the normal operating cycle if longer
questions.why: Ind AS 1: current if expected to be realised in, or intended for sale/consumption in, the normal operating cycle; held primarily for trading; within 12 months after the reporting period; or cash/cash equivalents unrestricted (with narrow exceptions). Otherwise non-current.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the 12-months-or-cycle dual condition is the standard MCQ AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Operating cycle OR 12 months — whichever is longer (for assets in the cycle); unrestricted cash is always current.

questions.q: A provision for restructuring under Ind AS 1/37 requires:
o: A detailed formal plan AND valid expectation raised in affected parties
questions.why: Provision for restructuring only when committed: detailed formal plan + implementation started or expectation raised with those affected.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the two-limb commitment test Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: No provision until people can reasonably expect the axe to fall — plan plus valid expectation, both.

questions.q: Inventory destroyed by a flood after the reporting date (no year-end condition) requires:
o: Disclosure of the nature and estimate of financial effect as a non-adjusting event, if material
questions.why: Non-adjusting event: disclose nature + estimate (or state that estimate is impracticable); never adjust.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — adjust-vs-disclose discrimination at speed Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Year-end innocence ⇒ disclose; year-end guilt ⇒ adjust. Floods rarely confess before 31 March.

questions.q: Presentation and classification of items are changed only when:
o: A required change by an Ind AS, or a change yields reliable/fairer presentation, applied consistently
questions.why: Ind AS 1 basis: change presentation only per a standard's requirement or for reliable, fairer info — and consistently for subsequent periods.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the twin-conditions change gate AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Presentational surgery: only with a standard's consent or a demonstrable improvement — and once, forever.

questions.q: A post-year-end issue of shares for cash:
o: Non-adjusting event — no retro restatement; disclose if material
questions.why: Equity issued after year end is non-adjusting for that year's FS — no retroactive capital.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the equity-issuance example of non-adjusting Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Fresh money after the date can't back-date itself into last year's capital.
mem.link: Chapter 3 — Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements

questions.q: Under Ind AS 1, extraordinary items are:
questions.why: Ind AS 1 prohibits presenting any item as extraordinary — treat big items as ordinary-but-material with separate disclosure.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the prohibition-with-a-legacy-twist Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Nothing is special enough to leave the ordinary column — size gets a note, not a category.
mem.link: Chapter 3 — Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements

questions.q: A customer goes bankrupt AFTER the year-end; the receivable was already overdue BEFORE year-end. The bankruptcy event is:
o: Adjusting — write down at year end because the condition existed then
Adjust only if the auditor is told first
questions.why: A post-year-end event that confirms a condition existing at the reporting date is ADJUSTING (Ind AS 10): the deterioration pre-dated year end, so the write-down belongs to the old year.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the confirmatory-event test is Ind AS 10’s most-tested line Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.ti: TI: Ind AS 10 — adjusting after-YE bankruptcy
mem.tip: A funeral after 31 March for a patient already ill on 31 March — the balance sheet must attend.

questions.q: Individually immaterial but collectively material items must be presented:
questions.why: Ind AS 1: present separately when nature, function or materiality warrants; aggregate similar immaterial items to test collective materiality.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — aggregation principle one-liner AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Small items in one pocket become a line item; nature and size both vote.
mem.link: Chapter 3 — Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements

questions.q: The Disclosure of Accounting Policies amendments to Ind AS 1 and Ind AS 8 replaced which phrase in the disclosure requirement?
o: Significant accounting policies with material accounting policy information
Material accounting policy with critical policy estimates
questions.why: Documented amendment (effective for periods beginning on/after 1 April 2023): entities disclose MATERIAL accounting policy INFORMATION — an immaterial policy description need not be disclosed, but disclosure may still be material when used with other information; the word 'significant' was removed.
questions.trend: Traceable to a real, publicly-notified amendment/standard (documented fact), tested in ICAI style.
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — terminology flips invented by amendments are the safest first-attempt MCQs Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.ti: TI: Amendment — Disclosure of Accounting Policies
mem.tip: Materiality now governs the POLICY note — describe what matters, not everything you do.
mem.link: Chapter 3 — Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements

questions.q: The amendments clarifying classification of liabilities as current or non-current state that the right to defer settlement must exist:
o: Any time during the following year
At the end of the reporting period, with covenant conditions complied with at that date
questions.why: Documented amendments (IASB 2020 and 2022 covenants amendment; ICAI adoption effective for periods beginning on/after 1 April 2024): the deferral right must exist AT the end of the reporting period; covenants assessed at that date; classification is unaffected by events between the period end and authorisation (except certain settlement-for-extinguishment cases); 'settlement' means transfer of resources.
questions.trend: Traceable to a real, publicly-notified amendment/standard (documented fact), tested in ICAI style.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — covenant-timing mechanics are tailor-made for objective papers AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Rights are frozen at 31 March; springing clauses between that date and signature do not move the line.
mem.link: Chapter 3 — Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
